gloss: counsel, advise; consult; purpose, plan; counsel, plan
summary: To give counsel and to take it: the qal is to advise another (Jethro, Nathan, the elders, Ahithophel), and also to resolve on a course, so that “Yahweh of Armies has counselled, and who shall annul it?”; its participle יוֹעֵץ is the counsellor at a king's side; the niphal is to consult together, and of enemies to conspire. The noun עֵצָה is the counsel given, the plan or purpose resolved on, and the faculty of counsel that stands with understanding and might; above all scripture sets the counsel of Yahweh, which stands for ever, against the plans of men, which he brings to nothing. מוֹעֵצָה is a people's own devices, walked in instead of his. Biblical Aramaic has the same root as יעט, with Arabic waʿaẓa “admonish, give good counsel” showing ẓ behind the צ.

words.gloss: counsel, advice; plan, purpose; the faculty of counsel
words.summary: About ninety times. The counsel one man gives another, which is heeded or rejected; the plan a man or a nation resolves on; and counsel as a gift beside understanding and might. The brief's one “qal” token under this word (Isa 19:11 יֹעֲצֵי) is the verb's participle, cited there; its “a tree” (Jer 6:6) is עֵצָה “trees” of עֵץ, kept in that entry.

senses.definition: The advice one gives another as to what he should do, which the hearer may follow or forsake; the counsel of the elders, the wise, a friend, or Yahweh himself.

evidence.note: “The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who listens to עֵצָה is wise.”
“Hear עֵצָה and receive instruction (מוּסָר), that you may be wise in your latter end”: counsel parallel to instruction.
“Instruction (תּוֹרָה) shall not perish from the priest, nor עֵצָה from the wise, nor the word from the prophet”: counsel is what the wise give.
Rehoboam “forsook the עֲצַת of the elders which they had counselled him (יְעָצֻהוּ)”: counsel given, then forsaken.
Nathan to Bathsheba: “let me counsel you עֵצָה, and save your life”.
Absalom to Ahithophel: “Give your counsel, what we shall do.”
“The עֲצַת of Ahithophel which he counselled in those days was as if a man inquired of the word of God.”
“Yahweh had commanded to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to bring evil on Absalom.”
Ahithophel “saw that his עֵצָה was not done” and hanged himself.
David: “Make the counsel of Ahithophel foolish, Yahweh.”
“Give here your word and עֵצָה”: the tribes asked for their advice.
Wisdom: “you ignored all my עֵצָה and would have none of my reproof (תּוֹכַחְתִּי)”.
“The sweetness of a friend is from counsel of the soul.”
“Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked.”
“With your counsel you will guide me, and afterward take me to glory.”
“They soon forgot his works; they did not wait for his counsel.”
“They rebelled against the words of God and despised the counsel of the Most High”: his counsel parallel to his words.
“Your testimonies are my delight, the men of my counsel”: the law as his counsellors.
“Woe to the rebellious sons, declares Yahweh, who make a counsel, but not from me.”
“Bring counsel, do justice.”
“Instruction shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.”
“Men listened to me and waited, and kept silence for my counsel.”
“According to the counsel of my lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God.”
Ahaziah “walked in their counsel”, the counsel of the house of Ahab.
The prophet to Amaziah: “you have not listened to my counsel.”
The lords of the Philistines sent David away “by counsel”, on taking advice.
“Israel shall be ashamed of his own counsel.”
Of the Branch who builds the temple of Yahweh and rules as priest on his throne: “the counsel of peace shall be between them both”.

senses.definition: What one has resolved to do: a plan or purpose, of men or nations, which may be hidden, thwarted or brought to nothing; and Yahweh's purpose, which stands and is done.

evidence.note: “Many are the plans (מַחֲשָׁבוֹת) in a man's heart, but the עֲצַת of Yahweh, it shall stand.”
“Yahweh brings to nothing (הֵפִיר) the counsel of the nations; he frustrates the thoughts of the peoples.”
“The counsel of Yahweh stands for ever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations.”
“Declaring the end from the beginning … saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure (חֶפְצִי).”
“Calling … from a far country the man of my counsel”: the one by whom the purpose is done.
“This is the counsel that is counselled (הָעֵצָה הַיְּעוּצָה) concerning the whole earth, and this is the hand that is stretched out.”
“There is no wisdom and no understanding and no counsel against Yahweh.”
The nations gathered against Zion “do not know the thoughts (מַחְשְׁבוֹת) of Yahweh, nor understand his counsel, for he has gathered them as sheaves to the threshing floor”.
The scoffers: “let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it.”
“You have done wonders, counsels from far off, faithfulness and truth.”
“Wonderful in counsel, great in sound wisdom.”
Yahweh “confirms the word of his servant and performs the counsel of his messengers”.
“Great in counsel and mighty in deed.”
“Hear the counsel of Yahweh which he has counselled against Edom.”
The same, against Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar “has counselled a counsel against you, and devised a device”.
“Because of the counsel of Yahweh of Armies which he counsels against it.”
“Take counsel together (עֻצוּ עֵצָה), and it shall be broken; speak a word, and it shall not stand, for God is with us (עִמָּנוּ אֵל).”
“I will swallow up its counsel”: Egypt's plans.
“I will make void the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem in this place.”
“God had frustrated their counsel”: the plan of Sanballat's men to attack.
“Woe to those who go deep to hide counsel from Yahweh.”
“You know all their counsel against me for death.”
“The men who devise iniquity and counsel evil counsel in this city.”
“The counsel of the crafty is carried headlong.”
“Shine on the counsel of the wicked.”
“His own counsel throws him down.”
“Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?”: Yahweh's design in creation.
“You would shame the counsel of the afflicted, but Yahweh is his refuge.”
“May he give you according to your heart and fulfil all your counsel”: your purpose.
“How long shall I set counsels in my soul?”: plans turned over in distress.
“They rebelled in their counsel.”
Babylon “wearied in the multitude of your counsels”, with her astrologers.

senses.gloss: counsel, the ability to give it
senses.definition: Counsel as a gift of mind, named with wisdom, understanding and might: the capacity to see what should be done.

evidence.note: “The spirit of Yahweh shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of Yahweh.”
“A nation void of counsel (אֹבַד עֵצוֹת) are they, and there is no understanding in them.”
Wisdom: “Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom; I am understanding, I have might.”
“With him are wisdom and might; he has counsel and understanding.”
“Counsel and might for war”: the Rabshakeh's taunt.
“Is wisdom no more in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent?”
“Counsel in the heart of a man is deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out.”
“Plans are established by counsel; by wise guidance make war.”
“The wisest counsellors of Pharaoh, their counsel has become brutish.”
“Who has measured the spirit of Yahweh, or as the man of his counsel taught him?”: Yahweh has no counsellor; quoted in Rom 11:34.

evidence.locator: Psa.33.11, עֲצַת → βουλὴ; Pro.19.21; Isa.11.2; Isa.46.10; βουλή renders עֵצָה ×69

evidence.note: “I did not shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel (βουλήν) of God.”
Jesus “delivered up by the determined counsel and foreknowledge of God”: the counsel that stands (Isa 46:10).
“Who works all things according to the counsel of his will.”
“The unchangeableness of his counsel”, to the heirs of the promise to Abraham.
“The Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God for themselves”: as Psa 107:11.
“Who has known the mind of the Lord, or who has been his counsellor?”: Isa 40:13.

parallels.note: “Thought, plan”: man's many plans against Yahweh's counsel, and the thoughts of his heart beside his counsel.
“Might”: counsel to decide and might to carry it out.
“Instruction, discipline”, received as counsel is heard.

phrases.gloss: counsel a counsel, devise a plan

words.gloss: advise, counsel; resolve, purpose, devise; (participle) counsellor; (niphal) consult together, conspire
words.summary: About eighty times, in three stems. The qal is to counsel someone, or to counsel a thing: to resolve on it, whether a man's scheme or Yahweh's purpose; its participle יוֹעֵץ is the counsellor, an office at a king's side. The niphal is to take counsel with others, which enemies do to conspire; the hithpael once, of conspiring.

stems.gloss: advise, counsel; resolve, purpose, devise; (participle) counsellor

senses.definition: To tell another what he should do or what will come, so that he may act on it.

evidence.note: Jethro to Moses: “Listen now to my voice; I will counsel you (אִיעָצְךָ), and God be with you”, and the counsel follows.
“I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go; I will counsel you with my eye on you.”
“I will bless Yahweh who has counselled me; in the nights also my kidneys instruct me (יִסְּרוּנִי).”
Nathan: “let me counsel you counsel.”
“The counsel of the elders which they had counselled him.”
Hushai: “But I counsel that all Israel be gathered to you.”
Balaam to Balak: “Come, I will advise you what this people will do to your people in the latter days.”
Jeremiah to Zedekiah: “If I counsel you, will you not listen to me?”
“How have you counselled him who has no wisdom!”

senses.definition: The participle יוֹעֵץ as a noun: one who gives counsel, often a king's adviser by office, set beside judges, princes and kings.

evidence.note: “Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counsellor (יוֹעֵץ דָּוִד).”
“Ahithophel was the king's counsellor.”
“Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counsellor, a man of understanding, and a scribe.”
“I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counsellors as at the beginning”: counsellors parallel to judges.
The child born, the son given, is named “Wonderful, Counsellor (פֶּלֶא יוֹעֵץ)”, on the throne of David (Isa 9:6).
“Is there no king in you? Has your counsellor perished?”: counsellor beside king.
Among the stays Yahweh takes away from Jerusalem: “the counsellor, and the skilful craftsman”.
“The wisest counsellors of Pharaoh”: filed by BDB under the noun's key.
“Among these there is no counsellor, who when I ask could answer a word”: the idols.
“Where there is no guidance a people falls, but in a multitude of counsellors there is safety.”
“Plans fail without counsel (סוֹד), but with many counsellors they stand.”
“Deceit is in the heart of those who devise evil, but to the counsellors of peace is joy.”
“With kings and counsellors of the earth.”
“He leads counsellors away stripped.”
“Before the king and his counsellors.”
“They hired counsellors against them to frustrate their purpose (עֲצָתָם).”
“Zechariah, a counsellor with insight.”
Ahaziah's “mother was his counsellor to do wickedly”.
“Have we made you the king's counsellor?”
“One who devises evil against Yahweh, a counsellor of worthlessness.”

senses.definition: To counsel a thing: to decide on a course of action and plan it, of Yahweh's purpose, which stands, and of men's schemes, good or evil.

evidence.note: “As I have purposed (דִּמִּיתִי), so it shall be, and as I have counselled (יָעָצְתִּי), so it shall stand.”
“Yahweh of Armies has counselled, and who shall annul it? His hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back?”
“Let them make known what Yahweh of Armies has counselled against Egypt.”
“Who has counselled this against Tyre?”
“Yahweh of Armies has counselled it, to profane the pride of all glory.”
“I know that God has counselled to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel.”
“Aram has counselled evil against you.”
“The scoundrel … counsels wicked devices (זִמּוֹת יָעָץ)”; and in 32:8 “the noble counsels noble things”.
“You have counselled shame for your house.”
“Remember what Balak king of Moab counselled.”
“They only counsel to thrust him down from his height.”

senses.definition: To deliberate with others before acting: a king with his elders or princes, an assembly among themselves.

evidence.note: “King Rehoboam consulted with (וַיִּוָּעַץ אֶת) the elders … saying, How do you counsel me to answer this people?”
“By pride comes only strife, but with those who take counsel (נוֹעָצִים) is wisdom.”
“With whom did he take counsel, and who made him understand, and taught him the path of justice?”: Yahweh consults no one.
“The king took counsel and made two calves of gold.”
The king of Aram “consulted with his servants”.
“David consulted with the commanders of thousands and of hundreds.”
“The king and his princes and all the assembly in Jerusalem took counsel to keep the Passover in the second month.”
Hezekiah “took counsel with his princes” to stop the waters.
Sanballat: “Come now, and let us take counsel together.”
“Let them take counsel together: who declared this from of old? Was it not I, Yahweh?”

senses.definition: To take counsel together against someone: to plot.

evidence.note: “They have consulted together with one heart; against you they make a covenant.”
“My enemies speak against me, and those who watch for my soul consult together, saying, God has forsaken him.”

senses.definition: To plot together against Yahweh's people.

evidence.note: “Against your people they make crafty counsel (יַעֲרִימוּ סוֹד), and they consult together (וְיִתְיָעֲצוּ) against your hidden ones.”

evidence.locator: Isa.14.24, יָעַצְתִּי → βεβούλευμαι; Isa.14.27 → βεβούλευται; Psa.83.4, 6 → ἐβουλεύσαντο; 1Ki.12.6 נוֹעָצִים → βουλεύεσθε; βουλεύω renders יָעַץ ×33

evidence.note: “From that day they took counsel (ἐβουλεύσαντο) to kill him”: the conspiracy of Psa 83.

evidence.locator: Num.24.14, אִיעָצְךָ → συμβουλεύσω; 1Ki.1.12; Jer.38.15; 1Ki.12.8, 13 יְעָצֻהוּ → συνεβουλεύσαντο

evidence.note: “I counsel (συμβουλεύω) you to buy from me gold refined by fire.”
“Caiaphas was the one who had counselled the Jews that it was expedient that one man should die for the people.”
“They consulted together (συνεβουλεύσαντο) to take Jesus by stealth and kill him.”

evidence.locator: Job.12.17, יוֹעֲצִים → βουλευτάς; Job.3.14 יֹעֲצֵי → βουλευτῶν

evidence.note: Joseph of Arimathea, “an honourable counsellor, who also waited for the kingdom of God”.

parallels.note: “Instruct, discipline”: Yahweh's counsel parallel to the instruction of the kidneys.
“Teach”, with הִשְׂכִּיל “instruct”: Yahweh's counsel as teaching in the way.
“Purpose, intend”: Yahweh's purposing beside his counselling.
Judges beside counsellors, as the leaders of the restored city.

opposites.note: “Annul, frustrate” (hiphil): what Yahweh does to men's counsel and what none can do to his.

words.summary: Seven times, always plural. Six times it is a people's own devices, walked in instead of Yahweh's way, whose fruit they eat; once (Pro 22:20) it is good counsels written for the hearer.

senses.definition: The plans men make for themselves in the stubbornness of their heart, followed instead of Yahweh's counsel, and bringing their own ruin.

evidence.note: “They did not listen or incline their ear, but walked in their own counsels, in the stubbornness of their evil heart, and went backward and not forward.”
“So I gave them up to the stubbornness of their heart, to walk in their own counsels”, after “my people did not listen to my voice” (81:12).
“They shall eat the fruit of their way and be filled with their own devices”: because “they would have none of my counsel (לַעֲצָתִי)” (1:30).
“You have walked in their counsels”, those of Omri and the house of Ahab.
The sword “shall devour them because of their own counsels”.
“Let them fall by their own counsels.”

senses.definition: Sound counsel given to a hearer.

evidence.note: “Have I not written for you excellent things in counsels and knowledge?”

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, three times: the king's counsellors in Artaxerxes' letter, and the officials who consulted together against Daniel. Aramaic ṭ answers to Hebrew צ here, as in עֵטָא. BDB also files the participle as a noun יָעֵט (xj.ai.ab), counting the same three tokens; it is kept here as the verb's participle, as יוֹעֵץ is in Hebrew.

senses.definition: The active participle as a noun: the counsellors of the Persian king.

evidence.note: “Sent from before the king and his seven counsellors (יָעֲטֹהִי).”
“The silver and gold that the king and his counsellors have freely offered to the God of Israel.”

senses.definition: To take counsel together and agree on a course.

evidence.note: “All the presidents of the kingdom … have consulted together (אִתְיָעַטוּ) that the king should establish a statute”: a plot against Daniel.

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, once, the counterpart of Hebrew עֵצָה.

senses.definition: Prudent counsel, the wisdom to speak rightly in danger.

evidence.note: “Daniel answered (הֲתִיב) with counsel (עֵטָא) and discretion (טְעֵם) to Arioch”, when he came to kill the wise men.

cognates.gloss: exhort, admonish, warn; give good advice or counsel; (ʿiẓa, mawʿiẓa) exhortation, admonition, warning
cognates.note: First-waw verb, as Hebrew first-yod יָעַץ (originally *w-), and its noun ʿiẓa drops the w as עֵצָה drops the y. The sense is counsel urged on another, as the Hebrew qal's counsel given. Arabic shows ʿ (not ġ) behind ע and ẓ behind צ, the sound Aramaic writes ט (יְעַט, עֵטָא).

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2953, art. وعظ, وَعَظَهُ (n42134)
evidence.note: “He exhorted him, admonished him, or warned him … he gave him good advice, or counsel; and reminded him of the results of affairs.” Inf. n. وَعْظٌ and عِظَةٌ, “in which the ة is a substitute for the elided و”.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2953, art. وعظ, إِتَّعَظَ (n42135)
evidence.note: “He accepted good advice.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2953, art. وعظ, عِظَةٌ (n42136)
evidence.note: Syn. مَوْعِظَةٌ, “an exhortation, or an admonition, or warning”.
“Compare Hebrew יָעַץ (ya'áts, “to advise, to counsel”).”

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums: the verb of Biblical Aramaic יְעַט, used in the Targum of 1Ch 13:1 for the Hebrew niphal “David consulted”. Aramaic ט for Hebrew צ is the ṯ̣ correspondence.

evidence.locator: s.v. יְעַט (יָעַט), J00482, citing Targ. Y. Gen. XLII, 24 (to counsel); Ithpa. אִתְיָעֵט, Dan. VI, 8; Targ. I Chr. XIII, 1; Targ. Y. Gen. XXVII, 42
evidence.note: “To counsel … Ithpa. to take counsel, to deliberate, plan.”

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic noun answering to Hebrew עֵצָה; the Targum of Deu 32:28 renders “a nation void of counsel” with its plural.

evidence.locator: s.v. עֵיטָא, P00529, citing Targ. Koh. XI, 3; Targ. Y. Gen. XXXVII, 14; Targ. Y. Deut. XXXII, 28 (pl. עֵיטְיַן)
evidence.note: “(יְעַט) = h. עֵצָה, counsel, advice, order.”

doctrine.statement: Men make many plans, but “the counsel of Yahweh, it shall stand” (Pro 19:21); “the counsel of Yahweh stands for ever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations”, while he “brings to nothing the counsel of the nations” (Psa 33:10–11). He declares “the end from the beginning” and says, “My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure” (Isa 46:10); what he has counselled no one can annul (Isa 14:24–27), and “there is no wisdom and no understanding and no counsel against Yahweh” (Pro 21:30). He needs no counsellor: “with whom did he take counsel?” (Isa 40:13–14), which Paul quotes, “who has been his counsellor?” (Rom 11:34). Men's counsel against his people is broken, “for God is with us” (Isa 8:10); he turned Ahithophel's good counsel to bring evil on Absalom (2Sa 17:14), and the nations gathered against Zion “do not understand his counsel, for he has gathered them as sheaves to the threshing floor” (Mic 4:11–12). The apostles say the same of the cross, that Jesus was “delivered up by the determined counsel and foreknowledge of God” (Act 2:23), and that God “works all things according to the counsel of his will” (Eph 1:11), confirming his promise to the heirs of Abraham “by the unchangeableness of his counsel” (Heb 6:17). From the verses: God's purpose, declared beforehand in his word, is certain; the plans of men, even those set against it, are either overturned or made to serve it.

The one called “Wonderful, Counsellor” is “a child born to us, a son given to us”, who sits “on the throne of David and over his kingdom” (Isa 9:5–6). His counsel is given him: “the spirit of Yahweh shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might” (Isa 11:1–2), the shoot from the stump of Jesse. Yahweh himself takes counsel of no one (Isa 40:13–14). Jesus received the spirit at his baptism (Mat 3:16), and God gave it him without measure (Jhn 3:34); he said, “my teaching is not mine, but his who sent me” (Jhn 7:16), and “I can do nothing of myself; as I hear, I judge” (Jhn 5:30). Of the Branch on his throne the prophet says, “the counsel of peace shall be between them both” (Zec 6:13). From the verses: the Messiah is the counsellor because he is a son born of David's line on whom God's spirit rests; his counsel is God's, given him, not his own apart from God, and he will give it as king on David's throne.

note: Drafted 2026-11-19 from the brief for יעצ. Words: עֵצָה (j.ck.ab), the verb יָעַץ (j.ck.aa), מוֹעֵצָה (j.ck.ac), and the Biblical Aramaic יְעַט (xj.ai.aa) and עֵטָא (xj.ai.ac), filed with their own roots יעט and עטא. Left out: m.az.ap and m.da.ae, zero-token cross-references to מוֹעֵצָה; BDB's noun יָעֵט (xj.ai.ab), which counts the same three tokens as the Aramaic verb and is kept as its participle; the brief's “a tree” token of עֵצָה (Jer 6:6), which is עֵצָה “trees” in the ets entry; the Isa 19:11 participle יֹעֲצֵי filed under the noun's key is cited under the verb's counsellor sense. The Isa 36:5 and Pro 20:5 tokens are also counted by ets's p.em.ac. Not entered: the biform עוּץ “take counsel” (Jdg 19:30; Isa 8:10 עֻצוּ, p.bm.aa), keyed to root עוצ with the names Uz and Jeuz; it may be the same root (Anderson and Moser list *ʿwṣ “advise” beside *wʿṣ) and could join this entry with its own `root` if wanted. No personal names of this root found in TIPNR. Sounds: Arabic waʿaẓa and the Aramaic ṭ both show ṯ̣ behind צ; Arabic shows ʿ behind ע. Syriac: the Peshitta uses ܡܠܟ for counsel (SEDRA root 1065); no Syriac yʿṭ was found in SEDRA, and Payne Smith (OCR only) not searched further, so no syc cognate. Ugaritic, Ge'ez and South Arabian not checked. Wiktionary links Arabic وعظ to יָעַץ. Ps 83 and 62 cited in Hebrew numbering (Eng 83:3, 5; 62:4). Open questions: (1) whether עוּץ should join this entry; (2) the doctrine item messiah-counsellor keeps Isa 9:5's other titles out of the statement; check it says what you want.
